title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: within the notes on the divided-power De Rham complex, Grothendieck pauses for a 'universal algebra' digression. He asks which contravariant invariants F of simplicial sets, valued in an additive category and converting colimits appropriately, exist, and how they are classified. The previous page (Prop. 3) claims that F0: Ss^op -> (Ab.)^op, X |-> C.(X), is universal among colimit-commuting functors from Ss^op into additive categories with colimits. He then reformulates it with simplicial abelian groups replacing chain complexes, and generalises Delta to an arbitrary small category.

On this page he proves the general statement. Let Delta be any small category, ^Delta = Hom(Delta^op, Set) and ^Delta_ab = Hom(Delta^op, Ab). By dualising, B = A^op, the claim becomes the following: for every additive category A with small colimits, restriction along the abelianisation G0: ^Delta -> ^Delta_ab, X |-> Z(X) = Z^(X), gives an equivalence Hom_!(^Delta_ab, A) -> Hom_!(^Delta, A). Here ! means colimit-preserving.

The proof runs as follows.
(i) The right side is equivalent to Hom(Delta, A), by restriction to representables (Kan/Yoneda extension).
(ii) For a colimit-preserving phi: ^Delta_ab -> A and M in A, the functor X |-> Hom(phi X, M) turns colimits into limits. On a presheaf category it is therefore representable, which yields a right adjoint psi: A -> ^Delta_ab. Conversely, psi comes from some phi iff, for each X, M |-> Hom(X, psi M) is representable.
(iii) Write psi as lambda in Hom(A x Delta^op, Ab) = Hom(Delta^op, Hom(A, Ab)), with lambda(x)(M) = psi(M)(x) = Hom(Z(x), psi M). The representability condition at X = Z(x) says lambda(x) is corepresented by an object phi(Z(x)) of A. So the data is a functor Delta -> A, which gives the equivalence.

Conclusion: Z: ^Delta -> ^Delta_ab is the universal colimit-preserving functor from ^Delta into cocomplete additive categories. In modern terms, Ab-valued presheaves form the free cocomplete additive category on Delta. He conjectures ('sans doute') the same for any topos.

Specialised to the simplex category, this gives a 'Corollary (Dold-Puppe)'. The cosimplicial object n |-> Z(Delta^n) in sAb is the universal cosimplicial object in cocomplete additive categories, for colimit-preserving functors. Hence, via Dold-Kan/normalisation, the corresponding cosimplicial chain complex is universal for cochain complexes; this is continued on the next page.

The next page draws the moral. Colimit-commuting additive invariants of simplicial sets correspond to (co)simplicial objects or complexes K in A, via F(X) = Hom(C(X), K). 'Operations' Omega on such invariants correspond to objects L of Ab_* or Ab., via Omega(F) = Hom(L, K). Dually, the covariant case is written with tensor products.
errors: He writes Hom(Delta^op, A^op) ≃ Hom(Delta, A); strictly this is Hom(Delta, A)^op. The op is harmless because the equivalence is applied after dualising B = A^op, but the variance bookkeeping is loose.
He writes 'phi(x) ∈ A' where phi(Z(x)) (the object corepresenting lambda(x)) is meant.

The representability step ('transforms colim into lim, hence representable') tacitly uses that the source is a presheaf-type category and that A is locally small. This is fine here, but the argument would need more care for the claimed generalisation to an arbitrary topos (e.g. presentability/site conditions).

Passing from the universal cosimplicial simplicial abelian group to a universal (co)chain complex uses Dold-Kan in A. This needs A idempotent-complete, which holds automatically for cocomplete additive A, but the point is not stated.

ideas.what: Abelianisation Z: ^C -> Hom(C^op, Ab) is the universal colimit-preserving functor from a presheaf category into cocomplete additive categories; equivalently Hom_!(Hom(C^op, Ab), A) ≃ Hom(C, A).
ideas.modern_name: Free cocompletion of an (Ab-enriched) category / enriched Yoneda extension; Psh(C, Ab) as the free cocomplete additive category on C
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (Kan extensions, 1958); Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory (1982); folklore
ideas.where_published: Similar linearisation/abelianisation discussions occur in Pursuing Stacks (1983); the related Kan-extension formalism is in SGA 4 Exp. I

ideas.what: The cosimplicial simplicial abelian group n |-> Z(Delta^n) is the universal cosimplicial object in cocomplete additive categories; hence the universal cochain complex via Dold-Kan (attributed by him to Dold-Puppe).
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of sAb / Ch>=0(Ab) as free cocomplete additive category on Delta; Dold-Kan as an equivalence of free cocompletions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold-Puppe (1961) for the use; categorical formulation folklore, cf. Lack-Street, 'Combinatorial categorical equivalences of Dold-Kan type' (2015)

ideas.what: Conjecture that abelianisation of an arbitrary topos T -> Ab(T) is universal among colimit-preserving functors into cocomplete additive categories.
ideas.modern_name: Ab(T) ≃ T ⊗ Ab in Pr^L (presentable categories); 1-categorical analogue of Sp(X) ≃ X ⊗ Sp (stabilisation as tensoring with spectra)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie, Higher Algebra §4.8 (∞-version); folklore for presentable additive 1-categories

ideas.what: Classification of 'operations' on additive colimit-commuting invariants of simplicial sets by objects of Ab_* or Ab. (Omega(F) = Hom(L, K)), as a universal-algebra framework apparently meant to characterise constructions such as the (PD) De Rham complex.
ideas.modern_name: Natural operations as corepresentable/Yoneda data; 'theories' of cosimplicial objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Yoneda); related to Dold-Puppe theory of non-additive functors

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly reads the Dold-Kan / Dold-Puppe correspondence as a universal property: sAb, and via normalisation chain complexes, as the free cocomplete additive category on Delta, with Z(Delta^n) as the universal cosimplicial object. This categorical reading is usually credited to much later work (e.g. Lack-Street 2015).
missed.quote: Corollaire (Dold-Puppe) : l'objet cosimplicial n ↦ Z(Δ^n_*) ... est universel pour les objets cosimpliciaux dans des cat. additives avec lim quelc.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only historical priority for a folklore viewpoint. The mathematics is standard enriched Yoneda.

missed.claim: He leaves unproved the remark that abelianisation is universal for an arbitrary topos. Its modern form, Ab(T) ≃ T ⊗ Ab in presentable categories, is known (and its ∞-analogue X ⊗ Sp ≃ Sp(X) is in Lurie).
missed.quote: Sans doute se vérifie pour un topos quelconque.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early instance of the 'stabilisation/abelianisation as tensoring' viewpoint. The result itself is now known, so the novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully proves a standard fact (Ab-presheaves are the free cocomplete additive category; Z(Delta^n) is the universal cosimplicial object) and frames Dold-Kan/Dold-Puppe as a universal property. The topos-level remark anticipates the 'X ⊗ Ab' viewpoint. All of this is folklore or later published by others, so it is of mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'commutant aux lim←' near the top should read 'commutant aux lim→' (inductive limits). The arrow under 'lim' in the handwriting points left, but the meaning is colimits throughout.
'donc φ(x) ∈ A' is literally what is written, but the meaning is 'φ(Z(x)) ∈ A'. The handwriting appears to show a struck-through/overwritten symbol before (x).
Second display: Hom(Δ, Ab^o) — the image supports this reading; the line '[≃ (Ab^o)^* ≈ Ab_*^o]' has the marginal addition 'dans le cas qui nous intéresse'.
'Hom_!^{lim→}' — the superscript in the image appears to be a small 'ξ'-like mark (probably an abbreviation for 'lim→'), not a clear lim symbol.
